# Box 1. Illustrative re-analysis of publicly available datasets; not a clinical study

*Auto-generated by `scripts/research/render_box1.py` from `results/json/`. Do not edit by hand.*

We re-analysed FETAL_PLANES_DB, a widely used public benchmark for fetal standard-plane classification, and three external datasets. In the training data, the acquisition machine is entangled with the label: 'Other' (non-standard) frames make up 65% of Aloka images but 14% of Voluson E6 images (difference 51 percentage points, 95% CI 45–57). A model that sees no pixels at all, only the machine and operator, separates standard planes from 'Other' with an AUROC of 0.73 (95% CI 0.71–0.75) on test images from the same machines; adding frame geometry and on-screen text statistics raises this to 0.88 (95% CI 0.86–0.89). A standard image classifier (ConvNeXt-Tiny, macro-F1 0.89) recognised 'Other' frames on 95% of Aloka images but only 52% of Voluson E6 images. Contrary to the pre-specified prediction, 'Other' recall on the Voluson S10, a machine almost absent from training, was higher than on the Voluson E6 (92% (95% CI 89–95) vs 52% (95% CI 45–59)), close to the Aloka level: the missed 'Other' frames concentrate on the Voluson E6, the machine on which 'Other' was rare in training. On external data from other hospitals and devices, most errors were not anatomical confusions but rejections of valid planes as 'Other' (92%, 100% and 99% of errors on the Dutch, British and African sets). High benchmark accuracy alone does not show how a classifier will behave on another machine.

Word count: 224.

| 'Other' recall by machine (ConvNeXt-Tiny, FPDB test) | Aloka 95% (95% CI 94–97); Voluson E6 52% (95% CI 45–59); Voluson S10 92% (95% CI 89–95) (S10 − E6 +40 pp, 95% CI +32 to +47; S10 − Aloka -3 pp, 95% CI -7 to +0) | E6 |

Data: FETAL_PLANES_DB (Burgos-Artizzu et al. 2020; CC BY 4.0), HC18 / UCL landmark benchmark, African fetal planes (Sendra-Balcells et al. 2023; CC BY 4.0). Models: six legacy classifiers trained on the official FPDB training split (seed 42). Statistics: patient-clustered bootstrap, B = 2000.
